transcript: In Japan, a country of disasters Preparing for earthquakes and typhoons That may come at any time is indispensable Strengthening buildings and preparing evacuation plans That become standard responsibilities For national and local governments Preparation at home is all so important Emergency food, water, flashlights A well-maintained portable radio Keep these in an accessible place Children must be taught how to behave When an earthquake strikes First drop, cover your head And hold on under a sturdy desk After the shaking stops Turn off flames if it is safe to do so So that you do not evacuate barefoot Keep shoes by the bedside Deciding where the family will gather is also important if people are scattered at school, workplace and home Where will you meet? segments.text: In Japan, a country of disasters
Preparing for earthquakes and typhoons
That may come at any time is indispensable
Strengthening buildings and preparing evacuation plans
That become standard responsibilities
For national and local governments
Preparation at home is all so important
Emergency food, water, flashlights
A well-maintained portable radio
Keep these in an accessible place
Children must be taught how to behave
When an earthquake strikes
First drop, cover your head
And hold on under a sturdy desk
After the shaking stops
Turn off flames if it is safe to do so
So that you do not evacuate barefoot
Keep shoes by the bedside
Deciding where the family will gather
is also important if people are scattered at school, workplace and home
Where will you meet?
If this is not decided in the initial stage
you may be unable to contact one another in the confusion
As a mental preparation for disasters
there is a concept called normalcy bias
People want to think I will be fine
Even when a heavy rain evacuation order is issued
They think it's still fine and fail to escape
In time to overcome this
Except that if nothing happens that is good
And evacuate early
Take actions that you hope will prove unnecessary
That instinct saves life
Disaster preparation is a matter of planning and habit
The accumulation of small daily preparations
Becomes a great difference when the moment comes
Better safe than sorry
This old proverb remains an unchanged truth
